pool.text: Bartolomeu Dias arrived and named the local area Cape of Storms.
Francisco de Almeida was killed by the Goringhaiqua at the Battle of Salt River.
Jan van Riebeeck established a way-station and the Fort de Goede Hoop.
Britain captured the city before it was returned by treaty.
British forces occupied the Cape again following the Battle of Blaauwberg.
Slavery was abolished, freeing over 5500 slaves in the city.
A major hospital institution in Cape Town was founded and later gained fame.
The expansion of the Cape Town foreshore was completed.
The apartheid government introduced the Group Areas Act to segregate urban areas.
A library was established in Cape Town, hosting books in several sections.
The famous Gatsby sandwich was first served in the suburb of Athlone.
A hospital in Cape Town underwent a major extension with two new wings added.
Nelson Mandela made his first public speech from the balcony of City Hall.
UNESCO declared Robben Island a World Heritage Site.
The Cape Town Central City Improvement District was founded as the largest district.
A maritime hub in Cape Town handled thousands of ships and millions of tonnes of cargo.
The region including Kirstenbosch was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Cape Town International Airport opened a new terminal for increased air traffic.
The Law Enforcement Auxiliary Service has been operating in Cape Town public safety.
Cape Town was named the World Design Capital by industrial design societies.
